language.name: siṭaiṅga
language.speakers_note: Estimates run from 13 million (2006) to 16 million (2007). Because the sources disagree, the project states "13 million or more".
language.status: Not classed as endangered (Glottolog). Used in everyday communication, on television and radio, and in songs.

timeline.text: The coast was part of the early kingdoms of Samatata and Harikela. Some accounts place the harbour on a map of the 2nd century; this detail still lacks a reliable source.
Arab traders were using the port by the 9th century and set up a trading post.

Sultan Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah of Sonargaon brought Chittagong into his sultanate. Sources use 1340 for the start of sultanate rule, not for the founding of the city, because the port had already traded for centuries.
A Portuguese settlement was permitted in 1528, the first European enclave in the region. The port was known as Porto Grande.
The Mughals took the city and called it Islamabad, a name still used for the old town.
The East India Company took control in 1793. The railway arrived in 1865, and in 1928 the port became a Major Port of British India.

On April 2, 2018, a government committee decided to change the official English spelling of the city and several other places. Many residents objected, citing loss of tradition, confusion over certificates and harm to trade with partners who know the port by its earlier name. Press reports of the time describe a committee decision and mention no public consultation or vote. This project writes Chittagong, the name its speakers use.
Chittagong is the country's busiest seaport and, according to the sources used here, its second city. Millions of people in the region are reported to speak siṭaiṅga every day.

port.text: The Port of Chittagong handles more than 70 per cent of the country's export and import trade, about 3.1 million containers (TEUs) in 2020–21.

districts.name: Chittagong
districts.note: Chittagonian is the main everyday language here.

districts.name: Cox's Bazar
districts.note: Chittagonian is widely spoken here, with local varieties along the coast.

tiers: 8 in the country. Chittagong Division has 11 districts.
64 in the country, each led by a Deputy Commissioner.
The smallest rural unit of local government, about 4,500 in the country.
government.national: Bangladesh is a unitary parliamentary republic with a single parliament, the Jatiya Sangsad, of 350 members.

facts.text: Cox's Bazar has a sea beach described as the longest unbroken natural beach in the world. The source gives its length as about 120 km in one place and 150 km in another.
Himchari National Park, just south of Cox's Bazar town, was established in 1980 and has forests, grasslands and waterfalls.
The Karnaphuli River runs about 270 km from Mizoram to the sea at Chittagong, where the city's port sits at its mouth.
University of Chittagong was established on November 18, 1966. Its campus at Hathazari covers about 936 hectares (2,312 acres).
Mezban is a Chittagong feast and festival, observed as a festival since the late 1960s. The name comes from a Persian word meaning "host". The traditional meal centres on rice and beef curry.
The port handles more than 70 per cent of the country's export-import trade, about 3.1 million TEUs in 2020–21.
Saint Martin's Island, the southernmost part of the country, is known locally as Narkel Dweep (Coconut Island). It is described as Bangladesh's only coral island.

naming.text: This project writes Chittagong throughout. In April 2018 a government committee changed the official English spelling. The press reports reviewed mention no public consultation or referendum, and many residents objected. As far as these reports show, speakers of siṭaiṅga in the city were not consulted.
